title: Caste colours compared with the artwork
method: Direct visual comparison with the supplied 1600 by 1200 image. Qualitative hue judgments, not calibrated colour measurements. Clothing, lettering and background are classified separately.

comparisons.artwork: Grey clothing on George Floyd and the masked people; grey cameras, tower, monument and central faint lettering.
comparisons.limit: Grey covers many unrelated objects and the background; it does not select a unique text group.

comparisons.artwork: Dark reddish lettering in END POLICE BRUTALITY; other reds include protest paint, question marks, flag details and VS.
comparisons.limit: Dark red is not demonstrably mulberry in this image. Bright red marks must remain distinct from the proposed purple red class.

comparisons.artwork: STOP KILLING US is dark green. Green and turquoise also appear in the flag, Statue of Liberty and background.
comparisons.match: Clear match for dark green text; ambiguous for turquoise objects
comparisons.limit: The novel describes Beta Lenina wearing green in Chapter 4, so every green object cannot automatically be assigned Gamma.

comparisons.artwork: Biden’s jacket is brown with olive tones; the left pedestal and hair are tan or gold.
comparisons.limit: No clearly khaki word group is identifiable. Brown, tan and gold are not silently treated as khaki.

comparisons.artwork: BLACK LIVES MATTER and NOT ONE MORE; border glyphs, STOP, dates and transaction lettering also appear black.
comparisons.limit: Black contains several separate inscriptions. Their reading order is not determined by the caste colour.

unmatched: Yellow Order and stability and facial tracking boxes
Bright red question marks and monument paint
Turquoise or cyan Statue of Liberty and tower background
conclusion: Green, black and grey have visible overlaps. Mulberry and khaki are uncertain. The five caste colours do not account for all prominent coloured text. The central Bitcoin word lettering is predominantly black, so the palette does not visibly divide those words into five classes. No colour based word order or hidden phrase has been established.
